proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(m=|\Omega|\), enumerate \(\Omega=\{\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_m\}\), and identify a complete law with \(q=(q_1,\ldots,q_m)\in\mathbb R^m\).  The observable map is the finite linear map
\[
 (O_\#q)(o)=\sum_{i:O(\omega_i)=o}q_i,\qquad o\in\mathcal O,
\]
so \(p\) has \(|\mathcal O|\) coordinates summing to one, while \(q\) has \(m\) coordinates summing to one.  The causal target is not defined to be an observed-law regression: the object bounded here is the full-law functional \(V_\pi(q)\) from \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\), and \(\Theta_I(p)\) is its image over the separately defined compatibility fiber in \(\mathrm{def{:}identified\text{-}set}\).

We use finite-dimensional closed-set algebra followed by effective real elimination.  First,
\[
 \Delta(\Omega)=\left\{q\in\mathbb R^m:q_i\geq0\ (1\leq i\leq m),\ \sum_{i=1}^m q_i=1\right\}
\]
is closed and bounded.  Every cylinder marginal \(q_t(h,a,r,m',s')\) and \(q_t^O(g,a)\) is a finite sum of coordinates of \(q\).  Hence the equations \(O_\#q=p\) are linear in \(q\), the equations in \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}factorization}\) are linear in \(q\), and every equation in \(\mathrm{ass{:}weak\text{-}shadow}\) is a polynomial equation of degree at most two in \(q\).  There are only finitely many such equations because all alphabets and the horizon are finite.  It follows directly from \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}fiber}\) that \(\mathcal K(p)\) is a closed semialgebraic subset of \(\Delta(\Omega)\).  Thus \(\mathcal K(p)\) is compact, and it is nonempty by \(\mathrm{ass{:}model\text{-}compatibility}\).

By \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\), every denominator in
\[
 \rho_t^\pi(\omega_i)=\prod_{u=1}^t
 \frac{\pi_u(A_u(\omega_i)\mid H_u^F(\omega_i))}
 {\mu_u(A_u(\omega_i)\mid H_u^O(\omega_i))}
\]
is at least \(\epsilon>0\).  Therefore the numbers
\[
 c_i=\sum_{t=1}^H\rho_t^\pi(\omega_i)R_t(\omega_i),\qquad 1\leq i\leq m,
\]
are finite fixed real coefficients.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\),
\[
 V_\pi(q)=\sum_{i=1}^m c_iq_i,
\]
so \(V_\pi\) is linear and continuous on \(\mathcal K(p)\).  Its graph over the fiber,
\[
 \Gamma_p=\left\{(q,v)\in\mathbb R^{m+1}:q\in\mathcal K(p),\ v-\sum_{i=1}^m c_iq_i=0\right\},
\]
is semialgebraic.  The effective projection result \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\text{-}real\text{-}cad}\) applied to the \(q\)-coordinates shows that
\[
 \Theta_I(p)=\{v:\exists q\ ((q,v)\in\Gamma_p)\}
\]
is semialgebraic.  It is also compact because it is the continuous image of the compact set \(\mathcal K(p)\).

Finally, a continuous real function on a nonempty compact set attains both extrema.  Consequently there are \(q^-,q^+\in\mathcal K(p)\) such that
\[
 V_\pi(q^-)=\min_{q\in\mathcal K(p)}V_\pi(q)=L(p),\qquad
 V_\pi(q^+)=\max_{q\in\mathcal K(p)}V_\pi(q)=U(p),
\]
where the last equalities are \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoints}\).  Membership of \(q^-\) and \(q^+\) in \(\mathcal K(p)\) is, by \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}fiber}\), exactly normalization and nonnegativity together with observed-cell marginalization, the known behavior equations, and every weak-shadow cross-product equation.  Thus these are attained sharp endpoints of the full-law image, not merely outer numerical bounds.

The technique is the elementary min-of-a-sum inequality together with the equality conditions for a finite sum of nonnegative terms.  By \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}attainment}\), the nonempty fiber \(\mathcal K(p)\) is compact and every continuous \(\ell_t\) attains its minimum and maximum.  Hence all quantities in \(\mathrm{def{:}stagewise\text{-}projection}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoints}\) are finite and attained.

For every \(q\in\mathcal K(p)\) and every \(t\in\mathcal T\), the definition of the stagewise extrema gives
\[
 \ell_t^-(p)\leq \ell_t(q)\leq\ell_t^+(p).
\]
Summing over the finite set \(\mathcal T\) and using \(V_\pi(q)=\sum_t\ell_t(q)\) yields
\[
 L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\sum_t\ell_t^-(p)\leq V_\pi(q)\leq
 \sum_t\ell_t^+(p)=U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p).
\]
Taking the minimum and maximum over \(q\in\mathcal K(p)\) proves
\[
 L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\leq L(p)\leq U(p)\leq U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p).
\]

Suppose first that \(\mathfrak F^-(p)\neq\varnothing\), and choose \(q_0\in\mathfrak F^-(p)\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}extremizing\text{-}faces}\), \(\ell_t(q_0)=\ell_t^-(p)\) for every \(t\), whence
\[
 V_\pi(q_0)=\sum_t\ell_t^-(p)=L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p).
\]
The preceding lower bound then implies \(L(p)=L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\).

Conversely, suppose \(L(p)=L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\).  Let \(q^-\) attain \(L(p)\), as supplied by \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}attainment}\), and put
\[
 d_t=\ell_t(q^-)-\ell_t^-(p)\geq0.
\]
Then
\[
 0=L(p)-L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}d_t.
\]
Because this is a finite sum of nonnegative real numbers, \(d_t=0\) for every \(t\).  Thus \(q^-\in F_t^-(p)\) for every \(t\), and therefore \(q^-\in\mathfrak F^-(p)\).  This proves
\[
 L(p)=L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathfrak F^-(p)\neq\varnothing.
\]

The same argument with \(d_t^+=\ell_t^+(p)-\ell_t(q^+)\geq0\), where \(q^+\) attains \(U(p)\), proves
\[
 U(p)=U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathfrak F^+(p)\neq\varnothing.
\]
Finally, \(\mathrm{def{:}rectangularity\text{-}defect}\) and the already proved weak inequalities give \(\Delta^-(p)\geq0\) and \(\Delta^+(p)\geq0\).  If the corresponding common face is empty, the relevant equality is false; for real numbers a weak inequality together with failure of equality is strict.  Hence emptiness gives, respectively, \(\Delta^-(p)>0\) or \(\Delta^+(p)>0\).

We prove the proposed statement, which explicitly assumes \(\mathcal K(p)\neq\varnothing\).  This compatibility condition is needed because otherwise the Chen systems may be infeasible and the displayed endpoint minima and maxima are not defined.

Fix \(H=1\).  At the only decision time, \(H_1^F=H_1^O=S_1\).  Choose any \(q\in\mathcal K(p)\), which is possible by \(\mathrm{ass{:}model\text{-}compatibility}\).  Observed marginalization and \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}factorization}\) give, for \(p(S_1=s)>0\),
\[
 p(S_1=s,A_1=a)=q_1^O(s,a)
 =\mu_1(a\mid s)\sum_{a'}q_1^O(s,a')
 =\mu_1(a\mid s)p(S_1=s).
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\), this is at least \(\epsilon p(S_1=s)>0\).  Thus every action belongs to a positive-mass cell whenever \(p(S_1=s)>0\).

Fix such a cell \(C=(S_1=s,A_1=a)\), and for a candidate completion write
\[
 b_m(r,s')=\Pr_q(R_1=r,M_1=m,S_2=s'\mid C),\qquad m\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Observed marginalization fixes
\[
 b_1(r,s')=A_{s,a}[s',r],\qquad
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}b_0(r,s')=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s'].
\]
Put
\[
 \alpha_r=\sum_{u\in\mathcal S}A_{s,a}[u,r].
\]
The stated response-positivity condition says \(\alpha_r>0\) for every \(r\).  Conditionalizing the weak-shadow cross-products is legitimate because \(p(C)>0\); the common factor \(p(C)^2\) cancels.  Thus, for every \(u,s'\in\mathcal S\),
\[
 A_{s,a}[u,r]\,b_0(r,s')=b_0(r,u)\,A_{s,a}[s',r].
\]
Summing this equality over \(u\) gives
\[
 \alpha_r b_0(r,s')=A_{s,a}[s',r]\sum_{u\in\mathcal S}b_0(r,u).
\]
Division by \(\alpha_r>0\) is therefore valid.  Defining
\[
 w_r=\frac{\sum_u b_0(r,u)}{\alpha_r}\geq0
\]
yields the necessary representation
\[
 b_0(r,s')=A_{s,a}[s',r]w_r.
\]
Summing over \(r\) proves
\[
 (A_{s,a}w)[s']=\sum_r A_{s,a}[s',r]w_r
 =\sum_r b_0(r,s')=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s'],
\]
so \(w\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\).

Conversely, given any \(w\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\), set
\[
 b_1(r,s')=A_{s,a}[s',r],\qquad
 b_0(r,s')=A_{s,a}[s',r]w_r.
\]
These arrays are nonnegative, their nonrespondent shadow marginal is \(A_{s,a}w=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}\), and their total mass is
\[
 \sum_{r,s'}b_1(r,s')+\sum_{s'}\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s']=1
\]
by the observed conditional table.  Moreover, both sides of every weak-shadow cross-product equal
\[
 A_{s,a}[u,r]A_{s,a}[s',r]w_r.
\]
Thus the construction is sufficient.  It is inverse to the preceding map.  Since, at \(H=1\), no restriction contains variables from two distinct positive-mass \((s,a)\)-cells, assembling the conditional arrays with weights
\[
 p(S_1=s,A_1=a)=p(S_1=s)\mu_1(a\mid s)
\]
gives the claimed bijection
\[
 \mathcal K(p)\cong\prod_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}\mathcal W_{s,a}.
\]
Zero-mass states have all corresponding complete atoms equal to zero and introduce no extra coordinate.

The conditional reward mean associated with \(w\) is
\[
 \theta_{s,a}
 =\sum_{r,s'}r\{b_1(r,s')+b_0(r,s')\}
 =\mathbf 1^\top A_{s,a}\operatorname{diag}((r)_{r\in\mathcal R})(w+\mathbf 1),
\]
which is exactly an element of \(\mathcal J_{s,a}\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}static\text{-}chen\text{-}cell\text{-}program}\).  Substituting the cell factorization into \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\), and using \(\mu_1(a\mid s)>0\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_\pi(q)
 &=\sum_{s,a}p(S_1=s)\mu_1(a\mid s)
   \frac{\pi_1(a\mid s)}{\mu_1(a\mid s)}\,\theta_{s,a}\\
 &=\sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}p(S_1=s)\pi_1(a\mid s)\theta_{s,a}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The cell coordinates vary independently and every displayed weight is nonnegative, so minimizing or maximizing the last sum is achieved by minimizing or maximizing each \(\mathcal J_{s,a}\) separately.  This proves the asserted value image and endpoint formulas.

Finally, if \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{s,a})=|\mathcal R|\) and \(w,w'\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\), then
\[
 A_{s,a}(w-w')=0.
\]
Full column rank implies \(w=w'\).  Compatibility supplies existence, so each \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\) is a singleton.  Since
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(A_{s,a})\leq\min\{|\mathcal S|,|\mathcal R|\},
\]
full column rank necessarily requires \(|\mathcal S|\geq|\mathcal R|\).  The product fiber therefore has a unique reward-completion coordinate in every positive-mass cell, and the displayed value image is a singleton.  This proves point identification.

We use exact sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition, with \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\text{-}real\text{-}cad}\) as the published classical substrate, and derive the specialization to the weak-shadow fiber.

Fix rational or real-algebraic \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\), every \(\mu_t(a\mid g)\) appearing in an importance ratio is nonzero.  The field generated over \(\mathbb Q\) by the finitely many coordinates of \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\), and by their permitted reciprocals, is therefore an effectively represented real-algebraic coefficient field.  In coordinates \(q=(q_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}\), membership in \(\mathcal K(p)\) is the conjunction of
\[
 q_\omega\geq0,\qquad \sum_\omega q_\omega=1,\qquad O_\#q=p,
\]
the finite linear behavior equations, and the finite quadratic weak-shadow cross-products.  Furthermore,
\[
 v=V_\pi(q)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 v-\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}q_\omega\sum_{t=1}^H
 \rho_t^\pi(\omega)R_t(\omega)=0
\]
is one linear polynomial equation over that field.  Hence
\[
 \Phi(v)\equiv\exists(q_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}\,\bigl[q\in\mathcal K(p)\wedge v=V_\pi(q)\bigr]
\]
is a first-order real formula with \(N\) real variables, \(s\) polynomial constraints, and maximum degree \(d\) in the presentation stipulated by the theorem.

Apply the sign-invariant CAD result \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\text{-}real\text{-}cad}\) to all input polynomials, ordering \(v\) as the uneliminated coordinate.  The algorithm terminates, performs exact arithmetic in the real-algebraic coefficient field, and produces an equivalent quantifier-free univariate sign formula for \(\Phi(v)\).  Its arithmetic-operation count is at most
\[
 (sd)^{2^{O(N)}}.
\]
Every examined CAD cell requires construction data, so the number of examined cells is bounded by the same asymptotic operation bound.

By \(\mathrm{def{:}identified\text{-}set}\), the truth set of \(\Phi\) is exactly \(\Theta_I(p)\).  A univariate quantifier-free sign formula can change truth value only at a real root of one of its finitely many nonzero projection polynomials.  Thus its truth set is a finite union of points and intervals with real-algebraic boundary points.  By \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}attainment}\), \(\Theta_I(p)\) is compact and hence closed and bounded.  After adjacent true CAD cells are merged, each connected component is consequently either a singleton or a closed interval, and every endpoint is real algebraic.

The exact CAD representation records each boundary root by a defining polynomial and exact sign or Thom data, so it gives exact endpoints.  For the enclosure alternative, let \(E\) be the finite set of distinct endpoints.  Exact comparison of real-algebraic numbers orders \(E\).  Because \(\eta>0\) and distinct members of \(E\) have positive separation, repeated rational bisection around each member produces rational intervals of width at most \(\eta\); refining further when necessary makes these intervals pairwise disjoint.  Exact sign evaluation at rational endpoints certifies that each interval contains its designated algebraic endpoint.  Reporting the paired endpoint enclosures, and the analogous enclosure for a singleton, gives the asserted certified \(\eta\)-description of every component.  This is a global value-image certificate: no local optimizer or convexity of \(\mathcal K(p)\) is used.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite family of \(s\) polynomials of maximum degree \(d\) in \(N\) real variables over an effectively represented real-algebraic coefficient field. A sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition adapted to \(\mathcal P\) can be computed, yields quantifier elimination for first-order real formulas using \(\mathcal P\), and has arithmetic complexity \((sd)^{2^{O(N)}}\).

source.verbatim_statement: For every finite set \(\mathcal P\) of polynomials in \(\mathbb R[X_1,\ldots,X_k]\), there is a cylindrical decomposition of \(\mathbb R^k\) adapted to \(\mathcal P\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the displayed CAD theorem in Saugata Basu, Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry: A Survey, arXiv:1409.1534; the locator also contains the stated \((sd)^{2^{O(k)}}\) bound and its quantifier-elimination consequence.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Sanity Corollary (one-stage Chen reduction). Let \(H=1\), suppose \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), and let \(S_2\) play Chen's always-observed \(F\) role. For every \(s\) with \(p(S_1=s)>0\) and every \(a\in\mathcal A\), behavior positivity implies \(p(S_1=s,A_1=a)>0\). In each such cell define the observed respondent matrix and nonrespondent vector from the observed reward, response, and shadow table by \(A_{s,a}[s',r]=p(M_1=1,S_2=s',R_1=r\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\) and \(\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s']=p(M_1=0,S_2=s'\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\). Suppose cellwise response positivity holds: \(\sum_{s'\in\mathcal S}A_{s,a}[s',r]>0\) for every \((s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\) and \(r\in\mathcal R\). Then the global fiber decomposes cellwise as \(\mathcal K(p)\cong\prod_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}\mathcal W_{s,a}\), where \(\mathcal W_{s,a}=\{w\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}:A_{s,a}w=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}\}\), and its value image is \(\Theta_I(p)=\{\sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}p(S_1=s)\pi_1(a\mid s)\theta_{s,a}:\theta_{s,a}\in\mathcal J_{s,a}\}\). Hence the endpoints are the corresponding weighted sums of the Chen cell-program endpoints. If every positive-mass cell matrix satisfies the precise full-column-rank condition \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{s,a})=|\mathcal R|\), necessarily with \(|\mathcal S|\ge|\mathcal R|\), then feasibility makes every \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\) a singleton and the one-stage value is point identified. This is the cell program of Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong, arXiv:2602.16061v1, source section titled \emph{Partial Identification via Linear Programs}, equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original claim invokes endpoint minima and maxima but does not assume that the compatible fiber, equivalently the product of Chen cell systems, is nonempty. Cellwise response positivity makes the odds parameterization well defined but does not imply \(\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}\in\operatorname{cone}(A_{s,a})\). Adding the frozen model-compatibility condition is therefore necessary and is a genuine feasibility restriction rather than the conclusion to be proved.

proposed.statement: For every \(p\) satisfying \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), the fiber \(\mathcal K(p)\) is a compact semialgebraic subset of \(\Delta(\Omega)\), the image \(\Theta_I(p)\) is a compact semialgebraic subset of \(\mathbb R\), and there exist \(q^-,q^+\in\mathcal K(p)\) with \(V_\pi(q^-)=L(p)\) and \(V_\pi(q^+)=U(p)\). Every reported endpoint is therefore attained by a full trajectory law reproducing the observed cells, the known behavior factors, and all weak-shadow cross-product equations.
proposed.justification: Attainment upgrades a numerical outer range into sharp policy-value endpoints supported by compatible data-generating laws.
proposed.gap: Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong, arXiv:2602.16061v1, source section titled \emph{Partial Identification via Linear Programs}, equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\), establish static cellwise sharp bounds; the present compact fiber is dynamically coupled and generally nonconvex because full-history exclusion is imposed by cross-products.
proposed.consumer: Clinical OPE analysts can report certified worst- and best-case deployment values without interpreting local-solver output as sharp.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The semialgebraic-image step uses the declared effective real CAD projection lemma, so the proof dependency must be explicit.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed statement requires the existing model-compatibility assumption explicitly, and its dependency metadata must match that premise.

proposed.statement: For finite alphabets and fixed rational or real-algebraic \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\) with \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), \(\mathsf{CAD}_\eta\) terminates on \(\exists q\,[q\in\mathcal K(p)\wedge v=V_\pi(q)]\) and returns all connected components of \(\Theta_I(p)\) as closed intervals or singleton points with exact real-algebraic endpoints; alternatively it returns disjoint certified rational \(\eta\)-enclosures of every component and endpoint. For a presentation with \(N\) real variables, \(s\) polynomial constraints, and maximum degree \(d\), classical sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition uses at most \((sd)^{2^{O(N)}}\) arithmetic operations, with exact coefficient arithmetic, and the same bound controls the number of cells examined.
proposed.justification: The result turns fixed-law sharpness into a terminating exact computation rather than a local numerical optimization claim.
proposed.gap: Duarte et al. (2024) motivate certified polynomial optimization for discrete causal models; this theorem specializes exact real elimination to the coupled weak-shadow value image and reports all connected components.
proposed.consumer: An auditor can reproduce exact algebraic policy-value bounds for a finite sepsis table or request certified enclosures at tolerance \(\eta\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Termination, real quantifier elimination, and the doubly exponential CAD complexity are the published classical substrate and must appear as an explicit dependency.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The coefficient-complete two-stage dossier remains open: no explicit rational observed atom table, affine pair \(q^0+B\lambda\), complete eliminated polynomial family \(M_j\), strict sign vector, exact endpoint calculation, or common-zero index set \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{eq}}\) is present in the frozen core, and this solve does not derive those coefficients.
open_obligations.obstruction: The compact-face criterion reduces strict containment to emptiness of a simultaneous stage-face system, while the signed-minor calculation only certifies a local objective slope. It does not show that locally forced opposite boundary choices are incompatible with one globally coupled complete-history law. Establishing that incompatibility on a relatively open observable region requires carrying out the specified elimination after choosing and verifying a concrete rational witness; the symbolic handles \(q^0\), \(B\), and \(M_j\) do not themselves contain that calculation.
open_obligations.attempted: I reduced both endpoint gaps to exact common-face emptiness formulas, parameterized each rank-two \(2\times3\) Chen block by its signed-minor null vector, and computed the continuation slope as \(c^\top z=G\). I also checked that exact CAD decides any fixed instantiated face system. These routes stop before the required cross-stage coefficient expansion and relatively open sign certificate.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The frozen core does yield the following exact, computable partial characterization.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}compact\text{-}face\text{-}pasting}\),
\[
 \Delta^-(p)>0\iff
 \neg\exists q\left[q\in\mathcal K(p)\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{t=1}^H\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^-(p)\right],
\]
and
\[
 \Delta^+(p)>0\iff
 \neg\exists q\left[q\in\mathcal K(p)\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{t=1}^H\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^+(p)\right].
\]
For a fixed rational or real-algebraic observed law and policies, \(\mathrm{thm{:}fixed\text{-}law\text{-}value\text{-}image}\) makes these emptiness assertions decidable by exact real elimination after the stage endpoints have been computed.

There is also a local observable slope certificate.  For a two-row, three-reward respondent block \(A\), direct cofactor expansion gives
\[
 A(D^{12},-D^{02},D^{01})^\top=0.
\]
If \(A\) has rank two, this vector spans \(\ker A\).  For a continuation coefficient row \(c^\top\), another cofactor expansion gives
\[
 c^\top(D^{12},-D^{02},D^{01})^\top
 =\det[(A_{0\cdot});(A_{1\cdot});c^\top]=G.
\]
Hence, on any feasible line \(w+\lambda z\), the local continuation objective is affine with slope \(G\), and \(G\neq0\) forces a local extremum to a feasibility boundary.  What remains unproved is the global elimination step showing, on one printed relatively open sign region, that the boundary choices forced at the two stages cannot be realized by one common complete-history law.
